source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — Day 90 print $4.426 (May 28, 2026), reported by AAA as '$4.42, down 12 cents from last week'; still the highest for the period in four years. Down from $4.491 on May 26 (Day 88) and the May 25 Memorial Day Monday print of $4.507, as falling crude on U.S.-Iran deal optimism (July WTI settled $88.68 May 27, a five-week low, -5.55%) fed through to the pump. +48.0% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline; ~18¢ below the June 2022 all-time record of $4.61. Patrick De Haan (GasBuddy): 'Average gasoline prices declined in [most] states over the last week as falling oil prices helped offset earlier price cycling in many markets… Much of the decline came after renewed optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran agreement pushed oil prices lower. While oil continued drifting lower on hopes of a deal, new CENTCOM reports involving U.S. defensive strikes highlight how quickly the outlook could change.' The ~2.5% May 28 crude rebound on renewed U.S. strikes near Bandar Abbas had not yet reached pumps. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown — Jeff Colgan): cumulative extra fuel costs to U.S. consumers since war start top $40 billion, more than $300 per household. Pump-price relief, if a deal lands, runs 2-3 weeks behind crude per De Haan.
